checks_run.procedure: Round-13 specifics: judge whether the D-026 stub rule (config_snapshot skips zero-length, untracked, non-symlink files) can hide a real configuration change. I extracted config_snapshot verbatim from the candidate runner, ran it in a disposable clone with HOME redirected to $TMPDIR, and applied the runner's own diff filter to seven cases.
checks_run.environment: disposable clone at 6c61f2e in $TMPDIR/stubprobe (removed afterwards); agent sandbox
checks_run.expected: stubs ignored; any real change to configuration reported
checks_run.actual: A (new zero-length stub) is ignored, correctly. B (new non-empty CLAUDE.local.md), C (a stub gaining content) and F (a tracked .gitignore truncated) are reported, correctly. G (a new empty file under .claude/) is ignored; an empty file carries no configuration, so that is acceptable. However, D (a non-empty untracked CLAUDE.local.md truncated to zero) and E (the same file deleted) are NOT reported, because the runner keeps only '>' lines. The deletion blindness predates D-026, and the stub rule extends it to truncation. The agent sandbox denyWrite and the write guard prevent agents from doing either, so this affects only the 'process outside the sandbox' detection row. Raised as Low finding F-DG0-012, which I would accept as an observation. The probe itself worked as intended (exit 0).
